title: Right Hand Limit
notes: **Definition:** A function f(x) is said to have the right hand limit l₁ at x = a as x approaches a through values greater than a (i.e., x approaches a from the right).
**Symbolic notation:** lim(x→a⁺) f(x) = l₁ means the right hand limit of f(x) at x = a is l₁.
**Alternative notation:** lim(x→a⁺⁰) f(x) = f(a + 0) — this reads as 'as x approaches a from positive side'.
**Concept:** We consider values of x that are slightly greater than a (like a + 0.1, a + 0.01, a + 0.001) and observe what value f(x) approaches.
**Direction:** The '+' superscript indicates approach from the RIGHT side (positive direction) on the number line.
**Geometric interpretation:** On a graph, we trace the curve from the right side toward x = a and observe the y-value being approached.
**Example:** For f(x) = |x|/x, as x approaches 0 from the right (x > 0), f(x) = x/x = 1, so lim(x→0⁺) f(x) = 1.
**Importance:** Right hand limits are essential for determining continuity and for analyzing piecewise functions.
confusion: Do not confuse right hand limit with the function value f(a). The right hand limit considers x approaching a, not x equaling a.
The notation x → a⁺ means x is getting closer to a from values GREATER than a, not from values less than a.
A right hand limit can exist even when f(a) is undefined — limits describe behavior near a point, not at the point.
For continuous functions, the right hand limit equals the left hand limit equals the function value, but this is not always true.
Don't confuse the notation: x → a⁺ (approaching from right) is different from x → +∞ (approaching positive infinity).
practice: Find lim(x→2⁺) (x² - 4)/(x - 2) by evaluating f(x) for x = 2.1, 2.01, 2.001.
For f(x) = ⌊x⌋ (greatest integer function), find lim(x→3⁺) f(x).
If f(x) = {x+1 for x > 2, x-1 for x < 2}, find lim(x→2⁺) f(x).
Sketch the graph of f(x) = sign(x) and find lim(x→0⁺) f(x).
Explain why lim(x→0⁺) √x exists but lim(x→0⁻) √x does not exist.
universalFacts: Right hand limits are one of two one-sided limits used to define the existence of general limits.
The concept of one-sided limits was formalized in the 19th century to provide rigorous foundations for calculus.
Right hand limits are crucial for analyzing discontinuities, especially jump discontinuities.
In physics, right hand limits can represent approaching a value from one direction (e.g., time increasing).
Many real-world phenomena have different behaviors when approached from different directions.
